finding: SIDES holds only new and old, so record refuses the whole batch when one reviewer finding has side context.
why: The forge change-comment verb allows context, so one finding can discard every other finding of the round.
fix: Accept context and post it on the new side, or name the limit and refuse only that finding.

finding: record answers next fix at the cap round, but no review round follows: begin refuses round-cap.
why: A caller that routes on next cannot tell that the fix has no later review.
fix: Answer a next value that says finish follows, when the round is the last.
evidence: return ok(round=number, cap=CAP, next="fix" if fix else "stop",

finding: _key hashes only the file and the finding text, so 2 defects in one file with the same words merge into one entry.
why: Two reports of 'missing null check' at src/a.py:10 and src/a.py:90 fold into one entry, and one defect is never fixed or posted.
fix: Keep the two apart when the same text repeats at another line in one round.

finding: The test for a low finding that returns as high does not check that finish posts it again.
why: Dropping the comment reset in _merge leaves the test green, and a blocking finding is then never posted at finish. unverified: reasoned from reading the test, not run.
fix: Run on to finish and assert the finding is in left.blocking with a url and a second forge call.

finding: No test has a deferred concern that runs in a later round, so the filter in _report is unpinned.
why: The only deferred case names a concern that never runs. unverified: reasoned from reading the test, not run.
fix: Defer a concern in round 1, run it in round 2, assert finish does not list it.

finding: call_forge has a test for a non-JSON answer only; the non-object answer and the missing ok branches have none.
why: A regression in those branches passes the suite.
fix: Add stub commands that print [] and {} and assert post_failed for each.

finding: A corrupt or foreign state file and an unknown finding id refuse bad-payload, which tells the caller its payload is wrong.
why: The payload is valid here and the state is wrong.
fix: Use a separate code for the state file and for an unknown id, and add both to the refusal table.
evidence: raise _bad(f"the state file {path} is unreadable: {error}") from None

finding: The refusal table omits bad-payload, so the exit-2 case has no next action.
why: A caller has to read the script to learn what to do with it.

finding: begin overwrites the stored change without a signal when a later call names another change.
why: A resume with the wrong change id posts later comments on another change.
fix: Refuse when the stored change differs from the payload.

criterion: error and rollback paths / status accuracy
finding: stopped_by is clean when an earlier round left a critical or high finding unfixed and the last round found none.
why: Round 1 fixes A and leaves B unfixed, round 2 finds nothing: a reader of the status alone sees a false all-clear.
fix: Return unfixed when any critical or high finding has that outcome.
evidence: if not any(entry["severity"] in TO_FIX and entry["last_round"] == done for entry in state["findings"]):

finding: An explicit side null is refused, and REVIEWER.md says side is optional.
why: A reviewer that emits side null fails the whole record with bad-payload.
fix: Read a null side as new.

finding: A posted medium finding that comes back high and stays unfixed gets a second comment with no link to the first.
why: The change then holds a stale medium comment and a new high comment for one finding.
fix: Keep the first comment's url in the entry, and name it in the second comment and in the report.
